tools.description:
Retrieve audio analysis

Returns what the clip sounds like and its musical timing map. `terms` and
`labels` describe the audio itself, as heard by a tagging model rather than
taken from the prompt: the voice, instruments, genre, mood and how polished
the mix is. Use them to check a take against what was asked for, or to
compare takes and pick one, e.g. for a video.

The timing map has every beat with its position in the bar, the tempo, the
meter, structural sections and the key. This is what syncing video to music
needs, e.g. cutting on every downbeat (`bar_position: 1`) or changing scene
where a section starts. Sections that share a `label` repeat the same
material, so a recurring label is usually the chorus. For word timings use
`GET /v0/audio/{id}/lyrics-alignment`.

Analysis is a separate model run, so it is not ready the moment the clip
is. The first request starts the run; it is not charged, and repeating it
does not start a second one. The beats (with `bpm`, `time_signature` and
`key`), the sections (with `duration_s`) and the description (`terms` and
`labels`) are separate runs, and each part is served as soon as its run
completes, even while `status` is still `processing`. A run that fails is
tried again, up to three times in all, so a part can arrive minutes later.

`status` is `processing` while a run is expected, in flight or due to be
tried again; poll until it leaves `processing`, typically within a minute.
It is then `complete` when at least one part succeeded, or `unavailable`
when none did. Either way no further run starts, so stop polling; a part
left empty or null failed every try. `key` can also be null when the key
could not be determined.

A song in the caller's own suno.com library is analysed too, for a token
with `library:read`, five at a time: the rest read `processing` until one
of those finishes.
tools.name: audio-analysis
tools.title: Retrieve audio analysis

tools.description:
Create a cover

Creates a new audio clip by covering an existing one with a new style or voice. The source must be `complete` (`400` otherwise). A voice always sings, so supplying voice_id keeps the vocals even with no lyrics. Signed in with Suno, the source may also be any suno.com song you may remix there: `404` if you can't see it, `403` if you can't remix it, `503` while it is still finishing. A cover takes its source's title unless you set `title`.

controls.description: Optional generation-control sliders, each a 0–1 fraction (suno.com shows the same values as 0–100%) but `variety`, a whole number 0–4. Omit a slider to leave the model's own default alone — there is no value that means "no change", so `0` is a real setting, not an unset one. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending one without it returns 403, and a value outside 0–1 returns 400.

audio_influence.description: How closely the result resembles the source clip's audio. Low reinterprets freely; high stays near the original.

style_influence.description: How strongly the `style` tags are followed. Low is loose interpretation; high adheres tightly.

variety.description: suno.com's Variety: how far the `style` tags are reinterpreted before the song is made. 0 Off (the tags as written), 1 Normal, 2 High, 3 Extra, 4 Max (a radical departure). A whole number; anything else returns 400. Omit it to keep the model's default. Signed in with Suno, it is not a paid feature.

weirdness.description: How far the result may drift from expected results. Low stays conventional; high goes experimental.

duration.description: Target length of the generated audio in seconds, 15–360. Omit to let the model choose. A value outside the range returns 400; the result is a target, not a guarantee.

idempotency_key.description:
Opaque key for safely retrying a creation request. Keys contain 1–255 bytes,
are scoped to the authenticated account across all supported creation
operations, and are retained for at least 24 hours. Repeating the same key
with the same operation and parameters returns the original resource and sets
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with different input returns `409`.
A replay never re-emits webhooks. Audio replays return the current clip

tools.description:
Generate audio

Generates a new audio clip in one of two modes. **Simple:** `description`
alone; the lyrics and style are written for you. **Custom:** `lyrics`, usually
with `style` and `title`. Mixing the modes returns a `400`: `description` takes
no `style`, and no `lyrics` unless `instrumental` is `true`. With
`instrumental: true`, `lyrics` and `description` may both be omitted. For a
suno.com user, simple mode can also work from up to 10 of their songs in
`reference_audio_ids`, to remix, sample, remaster, restyle, mash up or split
stems from them, or to edit one, with `description` saying what to do. For a
straight cover, extension or two-song mashup, the dedicated routes give more
control. Through MCP, a suno.com sign-in gets 2 songs per call, charged to their
credits, so confirm before making several calls at once; for a sound effect, a
loop or a sting of a few seconds, use sounds-create. Poll `GET /v0/audio/{id}`
for the result: the clip is playable once `status` is `streaming`.

controls.description: Optional generation-control sliders, each a 0–1 fraction (suno.com shows the same values as 0–100%) but `variety`, a whole number 0–4. Omit a slider to leave the model's own default alone — there is no value that means "no change", so `0` is a real setting, not an unset one. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending one without it returns 403, and a value outside 0–1 returns 400.

audio_influence.description: How closely the vocals resemble the voice supplied as `voice_id`. Only valid alongside a `voice_id` — a generation that conditions on no audio returns 400. Use the cover, mashup, or extension endpoints to influence a source clip.

style_influence.description: How strongly the `style` tags are followed. Low is loose interpretation; high adheres tightly.

variety.description: suno.com's Variety: how far the `style` tags are reinterpreted before the song is made. 0 Off (the tags as written), 1 Normal, 2 High, 3 Extra, 4 Max (a radical departure). A whole number; anything else returns 400. Omit it to keep the model's default. Signed in with Suno, it is not a paid feature.

weirdness.description: How far the result may drift from expected results. Low stays conventional; high goes experimental.

description.description: Natural language description; the AI generates lyrics and style. Simple mode: send it without `lyrics` or `style`.

duration.description: Target length of the generated audio in seconds, 15–360. Omit to let the model choose. A value outside the range returns 400; the result is a target, not a guarantee.

duration_guidance.description: Size AI-written lyrics to `duration` so short targets produce short songs (on by default when `duration` is set). Only meaningful with `duration` — sending it alone returns 400. Set false to restore length-unaware lyrics; custom `lyrics` are never rewritten either way.

duration_strict.description: Guarantee the clip never runs longer than `duration` (on by default when `duration` is set): generation is hard-capped at the target, so a song that would overrun is truncated at the cap instead of running long. Combined with the default duration-sized lyrics, most clips end naturally before the cap; a clip that does hit the cap ends abruptly rather than with an outro. Set false to keep `duration` as a soft target the model may overshoot. Only meaningful with `duration` — sending it alone returns 400.

idempotency_key.description:
Opaque key for safely retrying a creation request. Keys contain 1–255 bytes,
are scoped to the authenticated account across all supported creation
operations, and are retained for at least 24 hours. Repeating the same key
with the same operation and parameters returns the original resource and sets
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with different input returns `409`.
A replay never re-emits webhooks. Audio replays return the current clip
status from a live read.

instrumental.description: Generate an instrumental with no vocals. A voice_id always sings, so it takes precedence over this flag.

lyrics.description: Custom lyrics for the audio. Custom mode; not valid with `description` unless `instrumental` is `true`.

max_mode.description: suno.com's Max Mode: more compute to keep the song consistent throughout, at a multiple of the song's credits. Set it only when the user asks for Max Mode by name, and only on the songs they ask it for; never turn it on yourself to improve a song. Needs `lyrics` or `style`; with only a `description` it returns 400. Only for a suno.com user's song on a plan with Max Mode: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400, and a plan without it returns 403.

midi_upload_id.description: A MIDI score for the song to play, from midi-upload-complete (`POST /v0/midi/uploads`). Say how to use it in `description`, e.g. "a synthwave track that plays my melody", or send the score alone to have the song written from it; simple mode only, so no `lyrics` or `style`. Needs `model` `v6-wild`, which is the default with a score; any other model returns 400. It counts as one of `reference_audio_ids`' 10. As on suno.com, the song stays `queued` until a copyright check on the score passes, so it never streams early; a match fails it uncharged. Only for a suno.com user's song: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400.

model.description: Generation model label. Omit to use your plan's default. Labels beyond the default are granted per plan: an unknown label returns 400, one your plan does not hold returns 403. `GET /v0/account/usage` lists the labels you may send as `allowed_models`. If the user hasn't picked one, tell them which label you're sending, or that their default applies.

negative_style.description: Styles to steer away from (e.g. "polka, accordion"). Only valid alongside caller-supplied tags — sending it with `description` returns 400, since there are no tags of your own to steer. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending it without returns 403.

reference_audio_ids.description: Up to 10 suno.com songs for the AI to work from. Use it to sample or chop a song, remaster it, cover it in a new style, mash songs up, pull out or drop a stem (an instrumental, an a cappella, the drums), take inspiration from a song, or edit one: change a few words or lines of its lyrics, redo a time range, add or cut a section, or add or drop an instrument. A small edit keeps the rest of the song's own audio; changing words in more than 5 places re-sings the whole song as a cover. For an edit, pass just that song and send no `duration`, `instrumental` or `vocal_gender`, which make the song regenerate whole. Say what to do in `description`, naming the songs by title, e.g. "chop the vocal hook from Sunrise into a lo-fi beat" or "in Sunrise, change 'the light is gone' to 'the light came home'"; never put an id or link in `description`. Simple mode only, so no `lyrics` or `style`. Ids come from `GET /v0/library` (and its search and liked lists), a playlist, or a song made earlier; each must be finished, and the user's own or one suno.com lets them remix (else 403, or 404 if they can't see it). Only for a suno.com user's song: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400.

style.description: Genre and style tags (e.g. "jazz melancholic"). Not valid with `description`.

vocal_gender.description: Force the gender of the generated vocals. Omit to let the model choose. A `voice_id` takes precedence — a named voice already has a gender — and any other value returns 400. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending it without returns 403.

voice_id.description: ID of a voice to use, from POST /v0/voices. A voice always sings, so supplying one overrides instrumental. The voice must belong to your account and be "ready" — an unknown voice returns 404, one still processing returns 400. Signed in with Suno, it is instead one of your suno.com voices, from GET /v0/voices.

workspace_id.description: A workspace to file the new song in, from `GET /v0/workspaces`. Only for a suno.com user's song: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400, and a workspace the user may not add to returns 403.

tools.description:
Download audio

Returns a URL for one of the signed-in suno.com user's own songs, as `mp3`
(default) or `wav`, under suno.com's own download rules and download
credits. Requires the `audio.download` feature. Only for a suno.com user
whose token grants `download`; an API key gets 403.

Call without `confirm` first. If the answer is `requires_credit`, the
download would spend one of the user's download credits: ask the user,
and only with their approval call again with `confirm: true`. Any format
may answer `processing` while suno.com prepares the file, including for a
song that is still finishing; call again, no more than once a second. The
`audio-download` MCP tool waits out `processing` itself for up to about 50
seconds: if it still answers `processing`, call audio-download again, never
audio-wait.

`url` saves the file under the song's title. Hosts that show apps render a
download button for it; elsewhere, share or fetch `url`.

Refusals from suno.com carry a `reason` alongside `error` and `code`:
`quota_exhausted` (402, `insufficient_credits`), `no_permission` (403,
`forbidden`), `plan_required` (403, `feature_not_on_plan`), `invalid_asset`
(404, `not_found`), `format_unsupported` / `invalid_format` (400,
`invalid_request`), `rate_limited` (429, `rate_limited`; back off) and
`daily_limit_exceeded` (429, `quota_exceeded`; stop until it resets).

confirm.description: Spend a download credit if the song needs one. Send only after the user approves a `requires_credit` answer.

Only for a suno.com user whose token grants `library:write`; an API key gets 403.

Titles, lyrics and captions pass the same content check suno.com runs:

tools.description:
Create an extension

Continues the source clip (`id`) from `continue_at` seconds. The new clip
contains **only the continuation**, not the source followed by it — join the
chain with `POST /v0/audio/{id}/full-song` to get the whole song. The source
must be `complete` (`400` otherwise), and `continue_at` is relative to the
source clip's own audio.
A response with `clip_ids` made one continuation per id, each the end of its
own chain: extend or join the one you want, not both.
Signed in with Suno, the source may also be any suno.com song you may remix
there: `404` if you can't see it, `403` if you can't remix it, `503` while it
is still finishing. A chain that starts at such a song joins with `full-song`
like any other.

tools.description:
Get the whole song

Joins an extension (`id`) and everything it continues from into a single
track. The whole chain is resolved automatically, so you only name the last
extension. When an extension call returned `clip_ids`, name the one you
want: each is a separate chain end. Every clip in the chain must be `complete` (`400` otherwise), and
a chain is joinable up to 20 segments — the source plus 19 extensions. A
longer chain returns `400` and there is no partial join.

Signed in with Suno, a chain may start at a suno.com song you extended: the
join begins with that song and the songs it continues on suno.com, and
`concat_clip_ids` starts with its id; those earlier suno.com songs don't
count toward the 20. `404` if you can no longer see it,
`403` if you can no longer remix it.

Joining is free: no credits, no usage limit, since the extends that built
the chain were already metered. It is idempotent per chain — joining the
same chain again returns the first join's clip (with its current status)
instead of producing a second one, so retries are safe. A failed join can
be retried up to 3 times per chain; after that the failed clip is returned
instead of starting another job. A join that never reports back is retried
the same way once no worker could still finish it (30 minutes), which
also counts against the 3 attempts. Requires the same `generate.extend`
feature as creating the extension.

Poll `GET /v0/audio/{id}` for the result rather than blocking on the stream
endpoint — a cold join can exceed its wait window.

Opaque key for safely retrying a creation request. Keys contain 1–255 bytes,
are scoped to the authenticated account across all supported creation
operations, and are retained for at least 24 hours. Repeating the same key
with the same operation and parameters returns the original resource and sets
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with different input returns `409`.
A replay never re-emits webhooks. Audio replays return the current clip

tools.description:
Ask about audio

Asks a question about a finished clip. Suno's music agent listens to it
and measures it, then replies in text. Ask about anything you can hear:
the genre, mood and instruments, what the vocals do, how a section builds,
how polished the mix is, or how two parts compare. Tempo and key are
measured by Suno's own models. To get data back, ask for JSON and name the
fields, e.g. "End with a JSON block with bpm and key". The answer then ends
with a fenced `json` block holding those fields.

Returns a listen with `status: processing` at once. Read the answer with
getAudioListen (the `audio-listen-wait` MCP tool) by its `id`; it usually
takes under a minute. Nothing is made or changed and nothing is charged. A
caller may have five questions unanswered at once; one more is a 429
`concurrency_limit_exceeded`, and reading an answer frees its place. Past
200 questions in a UTC day, one more is a 429 `quota_exceeded`. The
answer never names a real artist or recording and quotes at most two lines
of lyrics. For a beat-by-beat timing map use audio-analysis, and for word
timings audio-lyrics-alignment.

Only a suno.com sign-in can call it; an API key receives 403
`user_principal_required`. A song in the caller's own suno.com library can
be asked about too, for a token with `library:read`.

question.description: What to ask about the audio. Name the fields you want when asking for JSON.

tools.name: audio-listen
tools.title: Ask about audio

tools.description:
Wait for an answer about audio

Reads a question asked with listenToAudio (the `audio-listen` MCP tool) by
the `id` it returned. `status` is `processing` until the agent answers, then
`complete` with the `answer`, or `error` with the reason. The
`audio-listen-wait` MCP tool checks every few seconds for up to about 50: if
it still answers `processing`, call audio-listen-wait again with the same id.
An answer stays readable for a day. Only a suno.com sign-in can call it; an
API key receives 403 `user_principal_required`.
tools.name: audio-listen-wait
tools.title: Wait for an answer about audio

tools.description:
Retrieve lyric alignment

Returns the clip's lyrics with the span of audio each word is sung over —
what a karaoke or caption display needs.

Alignment is produced by a separate model run, so it is not ready the
moment the clip is. Poll until `status` leaves `processing`, or subscribe
to the `audio.alignment.ready` webhook. The first request for a clip that
has no alignment yet starts the run; it is not charged, and repeating it
does not start a second one.

`status` is `complete` once the words are in hand (`words` is legitimately
empty for an instrumental), `processing` while a run is expected or in
flight, and `unavailable` when no alignment could be produced — a final
answer, so stop polling on it. Word timings are best-effort: a word the
aligner could not place carries `success: false` and a span inferred from
its neighbour.

A song in the caller's own suno.com library, for a token with
`library:read`, gets the alignment suno.com stored for it. No run starts
for one, so a song suno.com never aligned is `unavailable`, though one made
in the last ten minutes reads `processing` while suno.com aligns it.

status from a live read.

max_mode.description: suno.com's Max Mode: more compute to keep the song consistent throughout, at a multiple of the song's credits. Set it only when the user asks for Max Mode by name, and only on the songs they ask it for; never turn it on yourself to improve a song. Only for a suno.com user's song on a plan with Max Mode: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400, and a plan without it returns 403.

model.description: Generation model label. Omit to use your plan's default. Labels beyond the default are granted per plan: an unknown label returns 400, one your plan does not hold returns 403. `GET /v0/account/usage` lists the labels you may send as `allowed_models`.

negative_style.description: Styles to steer away from (e.g. "polka, accordion"). Requires the advanced- controls grant on your plan; sending it without returns 403.

workspace_id.description: A workspace to file the new song in, from `GET /v0/workspaces`. Only for a suno.com user's song: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400, and a workspace the user may not add to returns 403.

tools.title: Create a mashup

tools.description:
Transcribe audio to MIDI

Transcribes one of the signed-in suno.com user's own finished songs into a
multi-track MIDI file, as suno.com's Studio does. Any song in their library
works, including a stem. Requires the `audio.midi` feature (otherwise `403`
`feature_not_on_plan`), a token that grants `library:read` and
`credits:spend`, and a suno.com plan with Studio (Premier; otherwise `403`
with reason `plan_required`). An API key gets 403.

The first call starts the transcription and answers `processing`; call
again with the same id until `status` is `ok`, usually within a minute.
A transcription
costs 10 of the user's suno.com credits (none for a stem from suno.com's generative Get Stems), charged once when it finishes; a
song already transcribed, here or in Studio, is served again for free.
Tell the user the cost before the first call.

On `ok`, `url` downloads the `.mid` file under the song's title, and
`instruments` lists its tracks with how many notes each has. Hosts that
show apps render a download button for `url`; elsewhere, share it.
`failed` means the transcription errored and nothing was charged.

Refusals carry a `reason`: `plan_required` (403, `feature_not_on_plan`),
`quota_exhausted` (402, `insufficient_credits`), `invalid_asset` (404,
`not_found`, a song that failed to generate) and `not_ready` (422,
`not_ready`, a song still generating; call again once it has finished).
tools.name: audio-midi
tools.title: Transcribe audio to MIDI

tools.description:
Retrieve audio

Retrieves the current state of an audio clip. Poll after any creation call.
A generated clip is playable once `status` reaches `streaming`: play it
through `GET /v0/audio/{id}/stream`, or share `song_url` when it is present.
Keep polling until `complete` or `error` only when you need the finished
file or its duration. It reads one clip per call, by `id`; through MCP,
audio-wait takes several clips' `ids` at once.
tools.name: audio-retrieve
tools.title: Retrieve audio

tools.description:
Publish, unpublish, or allow or stop remixing of a song

Changes the settings on one of the signed-in suno.com user's songs, as the
controls on its suno.com page do. Send `visibility`, `can_remix` or both;
anything omitted is left as it is.

- `visibility: public` publishes the song: anyone can find it on the user's
  profile and in search. It is never entered in a remix contest. A song
  already streaming is held and published when it finishes, answering
  `publish_pending: true` with `visibility` still `private`; one not yet
  streaming is a retryable 409, so wait a moment or use `audio-wait`. A song
  suno.com won't let its owner publish, such as one with vocals from a
  source they can't publish, is a 403. Only publishes that succeed count
  toward 100 in a UTC day; past that, one more is a 429 `quota_exceeded`
  that changes nothing. `private` unpublishes it, withdraws it from any open
  remix contest, and is never capped.
- `can_remix: false` stops other users from covering, extending or mashing
  up the song; the user's own remixes are unaffected. More than 20 changes a
  minute is a 429. Refused with 403: a contest entry (its remix setting
  belongs to the contest), opening a remix of registered-catalog music to
  further remixing, and an account outside suno.com's remix feature. The
  error names which.

`can_remix` is applied first. If it succeeds and `visibility` then fails,
the error says `can_remix` was changed. Only the song's owner can change
its settings. Only for a suno.com user whose token grants `library:write`;
an API key gets 403.

can_remix.description: Whether other users may cover, extend or mash up the song.

visibility.description: `public` publishes the song, as suno.com's publish button does: anyone can find it on the user's profile and in search. `private` unpublishes it. Set it only when the user asked to.

tools.name: audio-settings
tools.title: Publish, unpublish, or allow or stop remixing of a song

tools.description:
Separate audio into stems

Splits a finished clip (`id`) into stems, as suno.com's Get Stems does: two
takes of the mode's parts, each stem marked with its `take`. `two` is vocals
and instrumental, 4 stems in all. `twelve` is the 12 parts (vocals, backing
vocals, drums, bass, guitar, keyboard, percussion, strings, synth, FX, brass,
woodwinds), 24 stems in all. A part the song doesn't have still completes, as
a near-silent stem. Each stem is an ordinary clip, so `GET /v0/audio/{id}`, the stream and
playback tokens work on its `audio_id`. Requires the `generate.stems`
feature. A stem can't be separated again, and the source can be at most
16 minutes long.

Only a suno.com user can call it for now; an API key receives 403
`user_principal_required`. Signed in with Suno, the stems are songs in the user's suno.com library and
the split costs suno.com's stem price in the user's credits: 5 per take for
`two` (10) and 25 per take for `twelve` (50), charged as each take's vocals
stem finishes. A take whose vocals stem fails costs nothing, and its other
stems are still delivered. The source must be a song in the user's suno.com library, whether
it was made through this API or on suno.com itself.

The split runs in the background: poll
`GET /v0/audio/{id}/stems/{group_id}` until `status` leaves `pending`,
typically within a minute or two. `partial` means some stems failed and
the rest are ready. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to retry
safely: the same key and source return the first group instead of
starting, and paying for, another.

idempotency_key.description: Opaque key for safely retrying the split. Reusing it for another source or mode returns `409` `idempotency_key_reused`; a retry while the first request is still running returns `409` `idempotency_in_progress`, so retry with the same key.

mode.description: `two`: two takes of a vocals stem and an instrumental stem. `twelve`: two takes of 12 stems. Both as suno.com's Get Stems makes them.

tools.name: audio-stems-create
tools.title: Separate audio into stems

tools.description:
Retrieve stems

Returns a stem group made by `POST /v0/audio/{id}/stems`. `status` is
`pending` until every stem has finished, then `complete`, `error`, or
`partial` when only some stems succeeded. Each stem's `audio_id` is a clip.
tools.name: audio-stems-retrieve
tools.title: Retrieve stems

Unlike a song

tools.description:
Complete an upload

Starts processing the file sent to an upload session's `upload_url` or
`upload_page_url`, exactly as `POST /v0/audio/uploads` would. Returns `409`
if the file is sent again while this call runs, and while no file has arrived: if the user is uploading through the page, wait
until they say it finished. Completing the same session again returns `409`
while the first call is still starting it, then the clip that call started.

Poll `GET /v0/audio/{id}` until `status` is `complete` or `error`.

title.description: Optional display title, replacing the one the session was created with.

tools.name: audio-upload-complete
tools.title: Complete an upload

tools.description:
Start an upload

Starts an upload whose file goes straight to storage rather than through the
request body. Use it for files too large to send inline, and whenever the
file's bytes are not at hand, such as a file the user attached in a chat.
Call it as soon as the user wants to use their own audio, before they attach
anything, so the uploader is where they drop the file.

When the user attached the file in this chat, pass it as `file`: the upload
starts at once and the response is the clip, as from
`POST /v0/audio/upload-sessions/{id}/complete`, with nothing left to send.

Otherwise the response holds the clip `id` the upload will become and two ways to send
the file, each good for one file for one hour:

- `upload_url`: send the raw file bytes in one HTTP `PUT`, for example
  `curl -T song.mp3 "<upload_url>"`. Quote the URL.
- `upload_page_url`: a page where the user picks the file in their browser.
  Give it to the user when you cannot read the file yourself.

If the user attached a file in the chat but you passed no `file`, or the call
refused it, and you can't `PUT` it yourself, still call this endpoint so the
uploader opens, then ask them to pick the same file there or at `upload_page_url`.

Both are credentials for this one upload, so share them only with the
person uploading. Once the file is sent, call
`POST /v0/audio/upload-sessions/{id}/complete`, then poll
`GET /v0/audio/{id}` as for `POST /v0/audio/uploads`. Formats and limits are
the same as that endpoint's. When the uploader reports the upload, carry on
with what the user asked for, such as a cover of it, without asking again.

This endpoint requires the `audio.upload` feature.

file.description:
The audio file the user attached in this chat. Pass the attachment
itself; the chat app turns it into this object.

title.description: Optional display title. Pass the file's name if you know it.

tools.name: audio-upload-create
tools.title: Start an upload

tools.description:
Wait for an audio clip to become playable

Call this after audio-create, audio-covers-create, audio-mashups-create,
audio-extensions-create or audio-full-song instead of polling audio-retrieve.
It checks every few seconds and returns the clip as soon as `status` is
`streaming` (the clip plays live and `song_url` works), `complete` or `error`,
or after about 50 seconds with the clip still pending. If it is still pending,
call audio-wait again. A creation that returned `clip_ids` made one song per id:
call audio-wait once with all of them in `ids`, so one player shows every song. Once
every one is settled it returns the first song's fields with every song, in order, under
`clips`, a clip it couldn't read as its `id` and `error`.
To hear how a finished song turned out, ask audio-listen.

id.description: Audio clip ID returned by a creation tool.

ids.description: Every clip ID a creation returned in `clip_ids`, instead of `id`. At most 12 per call: for more, call audio-wait again with the rest.

until.description: `playable` returns once the clip is streaming; `complete` waits for the finished file.

Finish uploading a MIDI file

Finishes a midi-upload-create upload once its file is sent. The file must be
a MIDI score with notes, under 256 KB; anything else is a 400, and a file not

Calling it again for a finished upload returns the same answer. Only for a

tools.description:
Start uploading a MIDI file

Starts uploading a MIDI file (.mid or .midi, up to 256 KB) a song can play
from: pass the finished upload's `midi_upload_id` to `POST /v0/audio`. Call
it as soon as the user wants a song from their own MIDI, before they attach
anything, so the uploader is where they drop the file.

When the user attached a MIDI file in this chat, pass it as `file`: it is
uploaded and checked at once, and the response is the finished upload, as
from midi-upload-complete, with nothing left to send.

Otherwise POST the file to `upload_url` as `multipart/form-data` within 10
minutes, every `upload_fields` entry first and the file last as `file`, for
example `curl -F 'key=…' -F 'policy=…' … -F 'file=@score.mid' '<upload_url>'`,
and call midi-upload-complete. If you can't send the file yourself, the
uploader shown with this call lets the user pick it; when it reports the
upload, carry on with what the user asked for without asking again.
`upload_url` and its fields are credentials for this one upload. Only for a
user signed in with Suno; an API key gets 403.

tools.description:
Generate a sound

Generates two short sound effects, one-shots or loops from a description, not
songs, as suno.com's Sounds does. Set `loop` for a seamless loop, and `tempo` and
`key` to fit it to a track. Both are ordinary clips, named in `clip_ids` — poll
`GET /v0/audio/{id}` for each. The model is chosen for you, and the length is up
to the model. Only a signed-in suno.com user can call it: the sounds land in their
suno.com library, each charged 1 credit like suno.com's Sounds. An API key receives 403 `user_principal_required`, and a
user on a suno.com plan below Pro (Free or Basic) 403 `feature_not_on_plan`.

description.description: What the sound is, e.g. "rain on a tin roof" or "boom bap drums".

idempotency_key.description:
Opaque key for safely retrying a creation request. Keys contain 1–255 bytes,
are scoped to the authenticated account across all supported creation
operations, and are retained for at least 24 hours. Repeating the same key
with the same operation and parameters returns the original resource and sets
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with different input returns `409`.
A replay never re-emits webhooks. Audio replays return the current clip
status from a live read.

key.description: Musical key, major or minor. Omit to let the model choose.

loop.description: Make a seamless loop rather than a one-shot.

tempo.description: Beats per minute. Omit to let the model choose.

tools.name: sounds-create
tools.title: Generate a sound

tools.description:
Generate speech

Generates spoken-word audio. Exactly one of `script` (spoken verbatim) or
`prompt` (the AI writes the words) must be provided. Providing `style`
alongside `prompt` returns a `400`. The result is an ordinary clip — poll
`GET /v0/audio/{id}`, and stream or mint a playback URL for it the same way.
Speech always generates on the default model, so there is no `model` to
choose, and no `instrumental` — speech is the voice. Requires the speech grant
on your plan.

backing_music.description: Keep a music bed under the speech. Default is no music at all.

duration.description: Target length of the generated audio in seconds, 15–360. Omit to let the model choose. A value outside the range returns 400; the result is a target, not a guarantee.

duration_guidance.description: Size AI-written words to `duration` so short targets produce short speech (on by default when `duration` is set). Only meaningful with `duration` — sending it alone returns 400. A `script` is never rewritten either way.

duration_strict.description: Guarantee the clip never runs longer than `duration` (on by default when `duration` is set): generation is hard-capped at the target, so audio that would overrun is truncated at the cap. Set false to keep `duration` as a soft target. Only meaningful with `duration` — sending it alone returns 400.

idempotency_key.description:
Opaque key for safely retrying a creation request. Keys contain 1–255 bytes,
are scoped to the authenticated account across all supported creation
operations, and are retained for at least 24 hours. Repeating the same key
with the same operation and parameters returns the original resource and sets
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with different input returns `409`.
A replay never re-emits webhooks. Audio replays return the current clip
status from a live read.

negative_style.description: Styles to steer away from (e.g. "polka, accordion"). Only valid alongside caller-supplied tags — sending it with `prompt` returns 400, since there are no tags of your own to steer. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending it without returns 403.

prompt.description: What the speech should say; the AI writes the words. Exactly one of `script` or `prompt` is required. The spoken-word instruction shares the engine's prompt budget, so the cap is 2947 characters, or 2887 with `backing_music`.

script.description: The words to speak, performed verbatim. Exactly one of `script` or `prompt` is required.

style.description: Delivery tags (e.g. "calm narrator, warm"), and the music bed's style when `backing_music` is set. Only valid with `script` — sending it with `prompt` returns 400.

vocal_gender.description: Force the gender of the generated vocals. Omit to let the model choose. A `voice_id` takes precedence — a named voice already has a gender — and any other value returns 400. Requires the advanced-controls grant on your plan; sending it without returns 403.

voice_id.description: Optional voice ID to speak in. Choose from the preset voices listed in the Quickstart, or, if your plan includes voice cloning, one of your own voices. The voice must belong to your account and be "ready" — an unknown voice returns 404, one still processing returns 400. Signed in with Suno, it is instead one of your suno.com voices, from GET /v0/voices.

workspace_id.description: A workspace to file the new clip in, from `GET /v0/workspaces`. Only for a suno.com user's clip: an API key or `test_mode` returns 400, and a workspace the user may not add to returns 403.
